column1: # Lane  Package that must not share its runner with other packages. Each reviewed lane is pinned to
# -p=1: one package at a time, so its tests own all four vCPUs. Two kinds of package live here:
#   - media certification: synthetic playout targets with strict latency or capacity assertions;
#   - CPU-heavy packages whose own parallel tests need a runner to themselves (#1570).
# Separate runners overlap the lanes without allowing package concurrency inside any of them. The
# highest lane number is the lane count (scripts/go-shard.sh); .github/workflows/ci-go.yml's matrix
# names each lane as certification-<lane>/<count>.
# internal/integration is here for balance. Its tests are serial, so it gains little from a runner
# of its own and keeps the lanes balanced when measured at -p=1. Weighed from real runs (#2007),
# app, api and playout came to 530s against store and integration's 369s, over the lane budget;
# app with integration and the rest together are 459s and 440s.
# internal/api serves the channel packager's HLS and MPEG-TS (#1512 phase 2c).
# internal/platform/store is CPU-heavy, not latency-sensitive: its SQLite tests run in parallel
# (#1631), and beside three other packages in an ordinary -p=4 lane they only competed for the same
# cores. Its migration tests replay every migration on purpose, and beside api and playout the lane
# passed the 15-minute timeout (#2716), so it has a runner of its own.
# schedule and demolibrary run their own tests in parallel: schedule's seasonal walks are hundreds
# of CPU-seconds of parallel subtests, demolibrary encodes filler and scans the tree. Sharing an
# ordinary -p=4 lane they measured 767s and 712s and timed it out (#2716). Alone at -p=1, dispatch
# run 42527652612 measured schedule at 251s with -race plus 179s without (it runs both), and
# demolibrary at 229s, so demolibrary joins api and playout and schedule has a lane to itself.
